species: mouse (C57BL/6; BV2 murine microglial cell line)
readout_other: ELISA (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-4); RT-qPCR; LDH assay; Iba1 and CD68 immunostaining; thermocouple temperature
direction_notes: Ultrasound reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines in LPS-treated BV2 cells in a frequency-dependent way (strongest at 2 and 0.5 MHz) and reduced hippocampal TNF-alpha and Iba1 optical density in LPS mice 4 h after treatment.
safety_notes: In vitro temperature rise below 2 C except 2.1 C at 0.5 MHz, 0.4 MPa, 60 min; LDH release reduced; k-Wave simulation gave skull temperature rise about 0.013 C for the in vivo parameters.

device.model: unfocused piezoelectric transducers, 0.5 MHz (44 mm), 1 MHz (23 mm), 2 MHz (23 mm)

timing.protocol_description: Single treatment of LPS-treated BV2 cells at 3 frequencies, 3 peak-to-peak pressures and 3 durations (5, 30, 60 min), duty cycle 20% and PRF 1 kHz; supernatant collected 24 h later.

exposures.label: Whole-brain sonication of LPS mice, 0.5 MHz

timing.protocol_description: 6 s sonication at each point of a grid (8.52 x 14.98 mm) covering the whole brain, 200 microsecond pulses at 1 kHz; a single treatment on day 7, brains collected 4 h later.

source_quotes.n_subjects: This study was designed as a pilot study and all animals were randomly divided into three groups: (i) saline <sub>n</sub> = 3, (ii) LPS <sub>n</sub> = 4 and (iii) LPS + ultrasound <sub>n</sub> = 4.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Mice received daily intraperitoneal injections of LPS or saline for 7 consecutive days to induce neuroinflammation and activate microglia (Fig. 5A)<sup>27</sup>. On day 7, mice in the LPS + Ultrasound group received a single whole-brain ultrasound treatment, whereas the saline and LPS-only groups underwent sham treatments.

source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: The parameters used were 0.5 MHz centre frequency, 0.2 MPa acoustic pressure, 1 kHz pulse repetition frequency, 200 μs pulse length, and 6 s sonication duration for each targeted point within a grid (8.52 mm × 14.98 mm) to cover the entire brain of the mouse (Fig. 7C).
source_quotes.exposures[1].free_field.pressure_kpa: To estimate potential temperature increases in our in vivo experiments, we simulated the propagation pathway ofour ultrasound pulses using a k-Wave MATLAB toolbox<sup>59</sup>. The anatomical skull geometry ofa mouse was derived from a publicly available micro-CT murine skull, voxelised and rescaled to match the simulation grid resolution of 0.231 mm, corresponding to 13 points per wavelength at 0.5 MHz<sup>60</sup>. The Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy number was set to 0.1 and the parameters of the simulations were set to 0.5 MHz centre frequency, 0.2 MPa pressure at the acoustic focus in water, 200 μs pulse length, 1 kHz pulse repetition frequency, and 6 s sonication duration.
